THE BIGGER PURPOSE: The Workflow page isn't just documentation. It serves two critical functions:

1. ENGINEERING FUNCTION: The tighter the workflow is documented, the smarter every new terminal session becomes at initialization. When an agent opens and reads this, it should understand exactly what tools it has, what hooks protect it, what rules govern it, and how to be maximally effective WITHOUT asking the user trivial questions. THE PAGE MUST HAVE TWO MODES:
- HIGH-LEVEL VIEW (default): Visual, collapsible, diagram-driven. Someone can scan it in 5 minutes. Think Apple keynote slides — clean visuals, minimal text, each section collapsed by default showing just the title + one-sentence summary.
- DETAIL VIEW (expand any section): Full technical documentation. File paths, code examples, configuration details. This is what agents read for initialization context.

Setup Checklist -> Agent Briefs -> Dispatch (via /prompts or auto-dispatch) -> Monitor (Dashboard + Campaigns page) -> Debrief (wins/losses/remaining) -> Retrospective -> Close
